content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"The highway is God's prepared way of salvation—chiefly the 'Highway of Holiness' of Isaiah 35:8 and the way prepared for the Lord in Isaiah 40:3-4—on which the redeemed travel home to Zion and from which the unclean/wicked are excluded; secondarily applied to John the Baptist's preparation for Christ, exilic return, sanctified living, and Gentile inclusion.","book_summary":"The Way of holiness: the prepared road home, made straight and smooth, where the wicked do not walk (Isa 35:8; 40:3-4).","consensus_core_identification":"A divinely prepared way of holiness/salvation by which God comes and the redeemed return to Him, closed to the unclean (anchored in Isa 35:8 and Isa 40:3-4).","book_core_identification":"The prepared, straightened road home—the Way of holiness—on which the wicked do not walk (anchored in the same two Isaiah passages).","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"SAME_CASES","boundary_disagreement":"None of substance. The book omits secondary consensus strands (John the Baptist application, Gentile inclusion, exilic-return typology), but omission in a terse glossary entry does not reject those cases; the central texts and identification are identical.","material_contradiction":"None. Both identify the highway as the prepared way of holiness for the redeemed, excluding the unclean/wicked, based on Isaiah 35:8 and 40:3-4.","rationale":"The book's entry reduces to exactly the consensus core: Isaiah's Highway of Holiness combined with the prepared/straightened way of Isaiah 40. Every element of the book's phrasing—'way of holiness,' 'prepared,' 'made straight and smooth,' 'road home,' 'the wicked do not walk'—maps directly to the KJV text of the two cited passages and to the primary meaning given by all four blind responses (holiness, exclusion of the unclean, redeemed returning). Differences are purely in compression and wording, not extension or referent, so this is a MATCH rather than REFINED.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue the book's exclusive focus on the redeemed's 'road home' quietly drops the equally consensus-weighted Christological reading (the way prepared for the Lord's own coming via John the Baptist), which might suggest a mild narrowing toward the believer's journey. But the entry cites Isa 40:3-4 itself, the very text underlying that reading, and a glossary's brevity is not a denial, so REFINED is not warranted.","confidence":"high"}
